newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita Elec to start global telecoms service.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita Elec to start global telecoms service.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Monday it will offer its domestic telecom services to a wider area this autumn and start offering international telecom services next spring by utilising existing internal telephone lines.

Matsushita plans to offer long-distance domestic telephone services to corporate clients at a cost below that of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), Matsushita officials told Reuters. The company's special telephone lines currently cover about 350 Japanese cities.
Matsushita will utilise International Telecom Japan Inc's (ITJ) international telephone lines to offer global telecom services to corporate clients, they said. ITJ is 8.9 percent owned by Matsushita.

The company's move follows Japan's planned lifting of a ban next spring that would allow companies to provide international telecom services by connecting special lines to existing public phone lines, they said.

A Matsushita spokesman said that the company plans to offer services to small and medium-sized corporations and not to individuals. The move was designed to effectively utilise the company's existing assets, rather than to make a grand entry into the global telecommunication business.
